Fixed declaration caches resize through original geometric expansions while retaining the old logical size, construct only after resize, publish the canonical declaration before INC, and record an interrupted INC explicitly. Validation errors retain the published cache reference. Finalization drains caches in original source order after eager fields and sorts, clearing only consumed references. Own abort removes the exact unacquired pending slot without fabricating DEC; source finalization refuses that interrupted acquisition. Cache backing is charged and released as actual Go manager-local reference storage.

Offset distinctness owns both default-constructed lexical offsets and both power/mod full-expression temporaries in the existing address-stable BV numeral continuation. Each matched operand copies the stored rational, reads width/base, computes power/mod, then copies the result back through the original const-reference assignment. Mod and power temporaries end before the next operand; final offsets drain in reverse order. Numeric children retain their exact invocation contexts on failure. Parameterized declarations retain original domain/parameter metadata, except concat discards parameters. Raw numeral factory borrows the caller rational, checks shape/types/zero width before numerical construction, and owns the original power/mod and p0/ps copies in the existing address-stable BV numeric frame. Zero recognition borrows the stored rational without copying or allocating. ownership: AST-owned address-stable numerical frame owns copied e_val and helper-local two. Direct division operates on e_val in place, increments count before the call in counting and after the call in removal, and retires each successful invocation completely before reusing that call site. Failed child contexts are retained for checked owning cleanup. Removal destroys two before nested NUM construction/publication; the copied numeral remains alive until caller exit. Exact nested constructor receipt joins before older DT. Actual cold numerical reservation campaigns retain source counts/output behavior and close shared graphs to zero budget.

Five lazy depth caches each own one reference per inserted expression. Depth zero performs no cache allocation or INC. Table construction precedes key INC; growth/insertion follows it. A refused insertion retains that exact pending INC for owning closure. Reset visits depths one through five and table buckets in source order, resets only size>=condition or condition zero, and records actual DEC consumption even when child deletion returns an error. Owning Close resumes that cleanup cursor without a second DEC. Successful cache hits read only key/hash/bounds, erasing numeral/child traversal. Fresh cold campaigns close cache/extraction/AST/numeric/symbol owners to zero shared budget.

The AST-owned address-stable c_val scope copies stored numerical metadata without normalization and holds that rational across subsequent AST calls through output publication. Nonnumeral default rational bookkeeping is erased. The unsigned numeral constructor is captured before entry, joined before older c_val DT and never retried at the same call site. Body and source-DT completion are separate; source readiness does not become true merely because owning cleanup ran. Successful scopes retire their exact invocation; failed scopes retain their actual plugin-list frame/context/header until plugin owning Close. Copied, ended, premature cleanup and uncaptured stopped-younger scopes reject. Actual Runtime campaigns refuse every reached read/constructor reservation until success and close the shared graph to zero budget.

Actual recursive call sites retain their entered structural frame and exact numerical invocation, captured before numerical copy/two/division allocations. Successful returns retire before loop reuse; failed call sites reject reuse after owning cleanup. Owning argument storage now uses native []ASTHandle: append acquires each reference, consumed-DEC cleanup retains unreleased roots on the actual frame. ADD ends tmp before arguments; MUL ends c_val then arguments then tmp; CONCAT ends arguments then new_last; equality ends out2 then out1. A stopped exact child blocks older source cleanup. Removed source vector placement/token/header/payload/push-growth receipts and the vector-to-slice bridge; factories borrow native roots directly. Reached frames remain on the owner list after body/source failure; owning Close drains youngest frames and actual numerical calls before older cache cleanup, preserving source history. Native slice storage adds no container/growth implementation credit.
deviations: The complete retained source unit is implemented with standalone checked Go owners that preserve pkg boundaries. Actual frames/numerical/reference owners remain charged; removal argument storage is native owning slices passed directly to factories, with no compact-vector bridge or simulated container growth. All ten retained bv-trailing TRACE/CTRACE sites have source-site Go records. Native stack/vtable/pointer/allocator/fatal/assertion/exception ABI is outside Go source-port credit, and Go returning-error cleanup does not claim native-fatal resumability.

Source edge behavior is retained: concat passes the full request to every child and can over-remove; an unknown child leaves new_last unchanged, so concat(x,zero4) removal of six returns four/null in release and reaches the full-width SASSERT in g3debug. Complete coefficient removal in MUL reaches is_numeral(null) before its zero-width guard; the Go boundary returns ErrASTHandle for that native invalid-pointer domain. ADD/equality VERIFY checks run in all source builds and a failed exact-removal check reaches release UNREACHABLE/undefined behavior; Go rejects that domain with ErrASTDomain and retains unchanged final output. These are qualifications, not repaired algorithms.

ownership: The partial sort path borrows the rational manager, copies coefficient numerals into typed owned buffer slots, sorts scalar IDs, then swaps each raw numeral with its source-indexed slot. A whole-slice raw swap transfers numeral ownership between the equation slice and buffer without cloning.

The concrete equation allocates its owner header first, copies coefficients into indexed reusable slots, transfers them into its vectors with sort_core, then owns its constant, integer coefficients and rational justifications. del_eq releases those in that order, leaving caller inputs and reusable buffers separately owned.

The pre-elimination setup borrows its rational manager, publishes variable metadata before the matching integer buffer slot, reserves that ID in a solver-local typed-slice priority queue, publishes a justification buffer slot before incrementing its ID, owns equation pointers in source list order, and closes its heap, rational and integer member buffers in reverse declaration order.

Solved-equation promotion transfers one equation pointer from the todo list to the solution list. apply_solution swaps integer and rational row storage through reusable owned numeral buffers; the old target row remains in its buffer until the next reset or solver destruction. The coefficient borrowed from that old row remains alive across the rational merge.

Non-unit decomposition borrows the selected positive magnitude, publishes a new parameter and buffer slot, compacts the todo equation's remainder numerals in place, copies auxiliary coefficients from the owned decomposition buffer into a solution equation, then substitutes that solution into prior occurrences. The decomposition buffer releases its copied numerals after the solution has independent ownership.
deviations: The source euclidean_solver_bug CTRACE guards at select_next_var:286 and solve:713 require a null selected variable despite a nonempty normalized equation list. Valid retained paths select a coefficient, discard empty zero equalities, or stop on a constant contradiction. normalizeQuery substitutes directly into the caller-owned c_prime, matching source constant publication before the rational justification merge. A real numeral allocation refusal in that later merge leaves c_prime at the substituted value while the solver retains the stopped normalization workspace for owning Close; the borrowed input constant is unchanged.

normalizeQuery retains its started equation-shaped m_norm_* workspace in the concrete solver owner after a stopped numeral copy. The original failure becomes a sticky solver stop; a later query cannot overwrite the partial owner. Successful queries release it at source function end, while solver Close drains it after the queue and before older buffer members. ownership: The mutable interval and node bounds own their fast-float endpoints; constant interval views borrow current node bounds. The context owns its root, parameter numerals and copied polynomial coefficients, and borrows the numeric manager and resource limit.

Fast inequalities own copied scoped fast-float values through their context. Clauses borrow atom pointers, count source-style references and register each watched variable once; context close retires the owning values after nodes. Learned-clause deletion and justification lifetime remain open.

Root close precedes source-order unit then problem-clause then lemma reference release; shared inequality values close at their last reference, and remaining unreferenced context-owned values close before context numerals. Idempotent release progress preserves cleanup retries.
deviations: The config_mpff tactic variable registration now grows source-order type/watch slots and the Go root bound arrays before initialization. The config_mpff root unit/definition/queue initialization and shared clause teardown are concrete. Selected bound justification tags are ported; node search/splitting, complete explanation ownership and the full solver lifecycle remain open.

The config_mpff six named parameter updates now retain source order, defaults, partial numeric mutation and a closable refused owner. The Go context allocates its root before this pass; complete constructor allocation order, node search/splitting and full solver lifecycle remain open.

The config_mpff context now displays definitions, units and clauses through the source MPFF to_rational_string spelling, which delegates to the ordinary String formatter. Borrowed variable display and shell forwarding are concrete; search remains open.

The config_mpff context now records child creation order, displays consistent leaves with inherited bounds and exact MPFF numeral text, and omits conflicting leaves. Search, splitting and statistics remain open.

The config_mpff round-robin variable selector and midpoint splitter now use concrete FastFloat arithmetic. Integer-bound normalization, directed unbounded splits and adjacent-value refusal preserve source order; the enclosing search queue, depth/node budgets and full tactic lifecycle remain open.

The config_mpff search loop now initializes the root, selects leaves breadth-first, replays child decisions, resumes canceled propagation, enforces depth/node limits and owns split children through cleanup. Fast and arbitrary-float checkpoints read their numeric Runtime when no shared process is bound, and read ProcessAccounting when it is bound; the pointer-free hardware context needs an explicit process binding. Standalone runtimes cannot include allocations from unrelated owners, and the complete tactic result/simplify lifecycle remains open.

Failed operations freeze the owner even when no receipt was acquired before refusal. Shrink releases removed coefficients forward before publishing shorter size. Named-root and direct/pooled physical campaigns verify failure cleanup.
